Consult Summary:
- Young adult female presented via telehealth with several days of constant, worsening lower abdominal (suprapubic, midline) pain rated 8/10, associated with light pink vaginal bleeding while using an Implanon implant; advised urgent in-person evaluation and to perform a pregnancy test today.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Constant lower abdominal pain (midline, below the umbilicus), present for a few days, worsening; severity 8/10.
  - Associated symptoms: light pink vaginal bleeding separate from menses; small amount of additional vaginal discharge; nausea without vomiting; constipation last week (now improved).
  - Function: able to continue regular activities (work, cooking), but pain can be very bad at times.
- Timeline:
  - Pain started a few days ago; progressively worsening.
  - Constipation occurred last week for about a week; this week “seems to be OK.”
- Gynecologic:
  - LMP ~2–3 weeks ago; reported as normal.
  - Periods irregular while on implant.
  - Sexually active; last intercourse 4 days ago (initially said 4 weeks, then corrected).
  - Contraception: Implanon implant inserted ~1 year ago.
  - Pregnancy test taken ~1 month ago; result not documented; no test since onset of current pain.
- Review of systems (pertinent positives/negatives as documented):
  - GI: nausea; no vomiting; constipation last week now improved.
  - GU: denies problems passing urine; denies pain on urination or strong odor; urinary frequency unclear.
  - Constitutional: denies feeling feverish; no faintness on standing reported.
  - Respiratory/others: no difficulty breathing reported.
  - Musculoskeletal: no shoulder pain reported.
  - Hematochezia/hematuria/weight loss: not confirmed (patient response unclear).
- Travel: abroad about a year ago; not recent.

Past Medical History:
- No prior surgeries reported.
- No prior pregnancies reported.
- No chronic medical conditions documented.

Medications:
- Implanon contraceptive implant in situ for ~1 year (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: amoxicillin.

Social History:
- Occupation: school teacher.
- Lives with husband and husband’s family.
- Tobacco/alcohol: not documented (patient response unclear).
- Recreational drugs: denies use.
- Recent travel: abroad ~1 year ago.

Family History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed (telehealth). No vitals recorded.

Investigations:
- None performed during this consult.
- Plan to perform a home urine pregnancy test today (result pending).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Lower abdominal pain with intermenstrual light bleeding; pregnancy status uncertain in a patient with Implanon.
  - Arrange face-to-face clinical assessment for abdominal (and likely pelvic) examination; patient to call support line to book.
  - Perform urine pregnancy test today; if positive, call back immediately for urgent assessment (to rule out pregnancy-related complications).
  - Safety-net: seek urgent care if pain worsens significantly, inability to keep fluids down, or other concerning symptoms develop.
- Issue 2: Recent constipation, now improved.
  - Monitor; no specific treatment initiated during this consult.
- Issue 3: Nausea without vomiting.
  - Supportive care as needed; no medications prescribed during this consult.

General Plan items:
- Maintain hydration and regular activities as tolerated.
- Follow up after in-person examination for further management based on findings and pregnancy test result.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: vital signs; full medication list and doses; comprehensive past medical history; full ROS; detailed gynecologic/obstetric history; STI risk assessment; urinary frequency characterization; pain modifiers (e.g., relation to meals/urination/defecation); immunizations; pregnancy test result.
- Internal conflicts: Age stated as “23 years old” vs year of birth 1996 (conflict noted). Last intercourse initially stated as 4 weeks ago, then corrected to 4 days ago.
- Transcript quality: multiple garbled/inaudible segments; some answers unclear or incomplete.
